card.name: Wording before treating an infection
card.fires_on: The word just before the treatment is named in infection-handling sentences, such as "appropriate" in "treated with appropriate local or systemic therapy", "directed" in "not directed against C. difficile", and "or" in "antifungal or antibacterial".

modes.label: appropriate before therapy
modes.description: The word "appropriate" comes right before an antifungal, antibacterial or local/systemic treatment.

modes.label: directed against C. difficile
modes.description: The word "directed" follows "antibacterial use not" in the C. difficile diarrhea warning.
modes.example: ongoing antibacterial drug use not<< directed>> against C. difficile may need to be

modes.label: antifungal or antibacterial
modes.description: The word "or" links antifungal and antibacterial agents for skin infections.
modes.example: an appropriate antifungal<< or>> antibacterial agent should be used.

card.plain: It fires on the wording that leads into treating a secondary infection, such as "treated with appropriate..." or "not directed against C. difficile".
